(In the school Yuri used to attend before joining the literature club…)

Ayano: “It’s hard to believe that Yuri joined a literature club, Kokona. And my sweet little Ayumi is growing up so fast, even if Yuri and I are single mothers…”

Kokona: “Yeah. Yuri was our best friend. I can’t believe that she left us for a literature club. Better than getting bullied by Musume, I guess.”

Ayano: “Agreed. So how’s your pregnancy with triplets going so far?”

Kokona: *laughs* “It’s definitely challenging, Ayano. Being pregnant with triplets is no joke. But, you know what? I’m actually enjoying it. It’s a unique experience, and I can’t wait to meet my little ones.”

Ayano: “That’s wonderful to hear, Kokona. I’m glad you’re embracing this journey. Have you thought about names for them yet?”

Kokona: “Oh, absolutely! My husband and I have been brainstorming. We’ve decided on Kaito, Haruka, and Sakura. We wanted something meaningful and beautiful for each of them.”

Ayano: “Those are lovely names, Kokona. I’m sure they’ll grow up to be as kind-hearted as their mother.”

Kokona: *blushes* “Thank you, Ayano. I hope so too. Parenting is a big responsibility, but I’ll do my best.”

(Just then, Ayano’s phone rings.)

Ayano: “It’s from Yuri! I wonder how her son Amatsu is doing. After all, Amatsu and Ayumi attend the same school, share the same birthday, AND are already 14 years old.” *answers the phone* “Hey, Yuri! Long time, no talk! How’s Amatsu doing at his school? I heard he’s in love with Ayumi now.”

Yuri: “Hey, Ayano! Yeah, it’s been a while. Amatsu is doing great at his new school. And yes, he has quite the crush on Ayumi. They’ve become close friends ever since they found out they share the same birthday. It’s cute, but it also makes me a little nervous as a mom.”

Ayano: “I can understand that. Having your child grow up and develop feelings for someone can be both exciting and worrisome. But I’m sure Amatsu will handle it well. He’s always been a sweet and considerate kid.”

Yuri: “Thank you, Ayano. I’m glad you think so. I trust that Ayumi will make the right choices too. It’s funny how our children are finding their own paths, isn’t it?”

Ayano: “It really is. Time flies so quickly. It feels like just yesterday we were all chatting and joking around in the school hallways. But now, our kids are growing up, and we’re experiencing new chapters in our lives too. Kokona wants to talk, too.” *hands the phone to Kokona*

Kokona: “Hey Yuri! How are you and Amatsu doing? It’s been too long!”

Yuri: “Hey Kokona! We’re doing well, thank you. Amatsu is settling into his new school nicely, and he’s been really excited about his friendship with Ayumi. They seem to have a special connection.”

Kokona: “That’s wonderful to hear. Ayumi has been talking about Amatsu a lot lately. She’s really happy to have a friend like him. It’s amazing how our kids are growing up together, just like we did.”

Yuri: “I know, right? It’s like history repeating itself in a way. I’m glad our children are forming their own connections and building their own memories. It’s a beautiful thing.”

Kokona: “Absolutely. Parenting can be tough at times, but seeing our children grow and thrive makes it all worth it. It’s a blessing to watch them become their own unique individuals.”

Ayano: “I couldn’t agree more, even though I’m already in my ninth month. We may have chosen different paths in life, but our friendship remains strong. And now, our children are creating their own bonds. It’s a beautiful continuation of our story.”

Yuri: “I’m grateful for that, Ayano. It’s comforting to know that our children have each other, just like we’ve always had each other. Our friendship has truly stood the test of time. And how many weeks along are you?”

this investigation of late Shang royal tombs of the Xibeigang cemetery takes a social interpretative archaeological perspective. Here, social-interpretative archaeology centres upon the reconstructive investigation of the intention and strategy adopted by those who conducted certain social practices (cf. Tilley 1994). Such intentions and strategies are ‘chosen’ from a repository of memories or customs that are preserved mostly in the form of ‘practical consciousness’ (i.e. internalised or embodied memories from which we decide how to handle certain social settings; see Giddens 1984: 41–45). To identify the archaeological evidence for such practical consciousness, we must situate the available evidence in the flow of time. The material traces of those past funerary occasions would have helped to preserve internalised memories, would have been referred to and would have been symbolically used in various manners and for various purposes in the practice (e.g. Mizoguchi 1993; <PRESIDIO_ANONYMIZED_PERSON> 1999: 193–97). At the Xibeigang cemetery, a ‘royal tomb’ is comprised of a rectangular main burial chamber with a sloping ramp attached to each of the four sides (Figures 1 & 2). Some tombs were built immediately in front of the designated ‘front’ of a pre-existing tomb (the ‘front’ being marked by the southern ramp in each case (strategy X). Those who participated in the funeral would have faced towards a specific pre-existing tomb, thereby effectively paying respect to both the person buried in that tomb and the person being buried (Figure 2). Interestingly, other tombs were constructed immediately behind the ‘rear’ of a pre-existing tomb. In those cases, the mourners turned their backs on the deceased, literally showing disrespect to the occupant (strategy Y), or putting themselves in the position of being respected by the deceased of the pre-existing tomb (strategy Y’ ) (Figure 2). Y and Y’ strategies have vastly different intentions behind them and we must, where possible, differentiate them from one another. In most cases, however, it may be difficult to specify which is which. There were also tombs located as if they were pairing with one another, although there must have been a gap between their construction. Here, it can be inferred that those who conducted the funeral at the later tomb intended to portray the person that they were burying as ‘equal’ to the person buried in the earlier grave (strategy Z) (Figure 2). Such strategic placement of the later tombs was made possible by the probable presence of an ancestral shrine. An ancestral shrine structure (F1) was excavated on the tomb of Fu-Hao   , and is assumed to be the ‘shrine of Mother Xin’—the posthumous name of Fu-Hao, recorded in oracle bone scripts (IA CASS 1980). Markers, such as low earthen platforms, probably also indicated the location of the main burial pit and the four ramps of the pre-existing tombs. Furthermore, as the edges of at least one of the ramps of a newly built tomb often overlap slightly with those of a pre-existing tomb (Figures 1 & 2), it is probable that the strategies were very carefully designed and pre-planned. It is, however, virtually impossible to prove whether it was the kings themselves who designed or planned such strategies prior to their death, or if it was those who conducted the funerary rituals. Through examination of the available evidence, we will attempt to verify this inferential hypothesis regarding the importance of ancestors and the cultic reproduction of kingly authority (Keightley 1999).

This study takes a social-interpretative archaeological perspective to investigate the late Shang royal tombs at the Xibeigang cemetery. The focus is on understanding the intentions and strategies behind the construction and siting of tombs, which would have been informed by practical consciousness or embodied memories of past funerary practices. The study identifies three key strategies: X, where a tomb is built in front of a pre-existing tomb to show respect to both the deceased and the person being buried; Y, where a tomb is built behind a pre-existing tomb to show disrespect to the deceased or to put the mourners in a position of being respected; and Z, where tombs are paired to portray the person being buried as equal to the person buried in the earlier grave. The study also suggests that such strategic placement of tombs would have been made possible by the presence of ancestral shrines and markers indicating the location of the main burial pit and ramps of pre-existing tombs. However, it is difficult to determine whether it was the kings or those who conducted funerary rituals that designed or planned these strategies, although the careful design and pre-planning suggest the involvement of both.

give code for app.py in flask
import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import json
from tensorflow.keras.preprocessing.text import Tokenizer
from tensorflow.keras.layers import Input, Embedding, LSTM, Dense, GlobalMaxPooling1D, Flatten
from tensorflow.keras.models import Model,Sequential
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import nltk
import random
from nltk.tokenize import word_tokenize
from nltk.stem import WordNetLemmatizer
from tensorflow.keras.preprocessing.sequence import pad_sequences
from tensorflow.keras.layers import Dense,Dropout
with open('data.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Preprocess data
lemmatizer = WordNetLemmatizer()
intents = data["intents"]

words = []
classes = []
documents = []

for intent in intents:
    for pattern in intent["patterns"]:
        tokenized = word_tokenize(pattern)
        words.extend(tokenized)
        documents.append((tokenized, intent["tag"]))
        
        if intent["tag"] not in classes:
            classes.append(intent["tag"])

words = [lemmatizer.lemmatize(word.lower()) for word in words if word.isalpha()]
words = sorted(list(set(words)))
classes = sorted(list(set(classes)))

# Create training data
training = []
output_empty = [0] * len(classes)

for document in documents:
    bag = []

    pattern_words = document[0]
    pattern_words = [lemmatizer.lemmatize(word.lower()) for word in pattern_words]

    for word in words:
        bag.append(1) if word in pattern_words else bag.append(0)

    output_row = list(output_empty)
    output_row[classes.index(document[1])] = 1

    training.append([bag, output_row])

random.shuffle(training)
training = np.array(training, dtype=object)

train_x = np.array(list(training[:, 0]))
train_y = np.array(list(training[:, 1]))

# Create model
model = Sequential()
model.add(Dense(128, input_shape=(len(train_x[0]),), activation="relu"))
model.add(Dropout(0.5))
model.add(Dense(64, activation="relu"))
model.add(Dropout(0.5))
model.add(Dense(len(train_y[0]), activation="softmax"))

model.compile(loss="categorical_crossentropy", optimizer="adam", metrics=["accuracy"])

# Train model
model.fit(train_x, train_y, epochs=1000, batch_size=8)

def clean_sentence(sentence):
    sentence_words = word_tokenize(sentence)
    sentence_words = [lemmatizer.lemmatize(word.lower()) for word in sentence_words]
    return sentence_words

def bag_of_words(sentence, vocab):
    sentence_words = clean_sentence(sentence)
    bag = [0] * len(vocab)

    for s in sentence_words:
        for i, word in enumerate(vocab):
            if word == s:
                bag[i] = 1
                
    return np.array(bag)
def chatbot_response(message):
    pred = model.predict(np.array([bag_of_words(message, words)]))[0]
    threshold = 0.25
    pred_class_idx = np.argmax(pred)
    
    if pred[pred_class_idx] > threshold:
        pred_class = classes[pred_class_idx]

        for intent in intents:
            if intent["tag"] == pred_class:
                response = random.choice(intent["responses"])
                return response
    else:
        return "I didn’t understand that. Can you please rephrase?"
while True:
    # Get input from user
    message = input("User: ")

    # Check if user wants to exit
    if message.lower() == "exit":
        print("Chatbot: Goodbye!")
        break

    # Get chatbot's response
    response = chatbot_response(message)

    # Print response
    print("Chatbot:", response)

records.prompt:
INTRODUCTION
Labour shortage is a significant challenge faced by various industries globally, which arises due to a gap between the requirement of skilled workers in a sector and the available pool of skilled workers (Manea, Virlanuta, & Muntean, 2019). This issue creates a demand-supply imbalance, leading to unfilled job vacancies and hampering growth potential for businesses and the economy. A recent report by the World Economic Forum (WEF) in collaboration with Adecco Group, outlining the top insights and trends of global labour markets, suggests that over 50% of businesses in different countries experience difficulty in finding candidates with the right skills, and approximately 16% of employers fail to find the suitable candidates (Adecco Group, 2023) and the healthcare sector is no exception.

The objective of this report is to analyze the causes of labour shortages, with a focus on the healthcare industry. Yet, it is not limited to this sector alone, and the report aims to explore factors such as restrictive immigration policies, rising economic inactivity, and the skills gap and evaluate how they contribute to the prevalence of labour shortages (Manea et al., 2019). Based on the analysis, the report intends to put forward recommendations to alleviate the issue of labour shortages and improve workforce availability in various industries.

The report aims to investigate the labour shortage phenomenon in the healthcare industry comprehensively, while analysing three significant causes of labour shortages. Finally, the report will propose research-based recommendations for addressing the identified causes. By shedding light on these pivotal aspects, this report shall provide useful insights to policymakers, industry leaders, and educational institutions to combat the pressing issue of labour shortages.


FINDINGS
1.Labour Shortages in the Healthcare Industry

The labour shortage in the healthcare sector is a pressing issue worldwide, with numerous factors contributing to the problem. Increasing demand for healthcare services due to an expanding patient population, coupled with an inadequate number of professional healthcare workers, further strains the system (Manea et al., 2019). This section will critically analyse the key challenges associated with labour shortages in healthcare, focusing on the ageing population, educational bottlenecks in training healthcare professionals, and the high levels of stress and burnout in the industry.

Ageing Population: Bai (2021) noted that the ageing population is a significant contributor to the shortage of healthcare workers. An ageing population leads to a rise in healthcare service demand and a decrease in the workforce as older professionals retire. Adapting the workforce to retain senior employees and attract younger professionals is crucial for providing evidence. However, this presents challenges related to work-life balance, workloads, and professional development opportunities (Manea et al., 2019). Addressing these challenges is crucial for ensuring a sustainable healthcare workforce. Hence, employers ought to adopt tactics that encourage the recruitment of younger professionals and enable the sustenance of older workers' careers, ultimately alleviating the adverse effects of an ageing population on the labour force.

Educational Bottlenecks: These are a significant factor in the shortage of healthcare professionals. Insufficient capacity and resources of educational institutions constrain the number of graduates who can enter the labour market (De Avila, 2019). High tuition fees may deter potential healthcare professionals (Nei et al., 2019), and as such, lowering tuition fees and improving healthcare education resources could potentially increase student enrollment in degree programmes. Addressing educational bottlenecks is crucial for ensuring a consistent supply of qualified healthcare professionals to the industry. Thus, addressing these challenges will enhance the healthcare industry's ability to handle staffing deficiencies.

Work-Related Stress and Burnout: The industry is also confronted with labour shortages as a result of work-related stress and burnout (Dyrbye et al., 2020). Rotenstein et al. (2018) observed that healthcare professionals are highly prone to experiencing burnout due to factors such as extended work hours, understaffing, and heightened patient demands. He also found that stress and burnout have a more significant influence on attrition rates in the healthcare field than in other industries. Employers in the healthcare industry must address the sources of stress and burnout among their workforce to effectively provide an explanation. Hence, prioritising stress and burnout mitigation in the healthcare sector can reduce attrition rates and better manage labour shortages.

The healthcare labour shortage is caused by a confluence of demographic factors, educational and training impediments, and work-related stress and burnout. It is imperative to conduct a thorough analysis of the influence of each contributing element in order to develop efficacious tactics for the recruitment and retention of healthcare professionals. Reducing tuition fees for healthcare degrees, investing in training and development, and prioritising worker well-being are potential strategies to alleviate the current labour crisis in the healthcare industry.

2.Restrictive Immigration Policies

Restrictive immigration policies serve as a considerable barrier to addressing labor shortages across industries, including healthcare. Immigrants have historically played a crucial role in filling workforce gaps when domestic labor pools are inadequate (Taylor & Walmsley, 2023). However, many countries have introduced stringent immigration policies in recent years, thwarting the influx of skilled professionals, including healthcare workers, and curtailing their ability to alleviate workforce shortfalls (Taylor & Walmsley, 2023). To ensure industries, including healthcare, have the labour force they need, policymakers must be aware of the impact of such policies and take steps to mitigate them.

A primary hurdle resulting from restrictive immigration policies is the non-recognition or devaluation of foreign qualifications and credentials (Ortega & Peri, 2019). In numerous countries, foreign-educated professionals must undergo rigorous local certification and licensing processes to practice within the jurisdiction, which can be time-consuming and expensive (Ruhs, 2022). Consequently, skilled professionals may become disillusioned by these challenges and abandon their ambitions of working abroad, causing a further strain on labor shortages.

Rigorous visa regulations and quotas can limit the number of skilled workers granted visas or impose extremely stringent applicant criteria (Chellaraj and Maskus, 2018). These regulations create significant barriers for international talent looking to work in other countries. The resulting restrictions limit the influx of skilled immigrants that are to potentially alleviate existing labour shortages. Therefore, to address long-term labour shortages, countries should consider revising visa policies to allow a larger pool of skilled international talent to contribute to their workforce.

Overall, restrictive immigration policies contribute to labour shortages by presenting barriers for skilled professionals attempting to work in other nations, specifically concerning healthcare workers. Obstacles include the lack of recognition for foreign qualifications, arduous and costly certification procedures, and limiting visa regulations. Through these hindrances, restrictive immigration policies jeopardize the ability of countries to address labour shortages in critical sectors, such as healthcare, by hindering the international mobility of skilled professionals.

3. Rising Economic Inactivity

According to Papachristos (2020) and Manea et al. (2019), the rise in economic inactivity has had a significant impact on labour shortages in sectors such as healthcare. Economic inactivity, referring to people who are not working and are not actively looking for work, is caused by factors such as an ageing population, early retirement trends, and long-term health problems. Kaufmann (2021), posits that a shrinking pool of potential workers has contributed to increased labour market pressure, resulting in numerous unfilled job vacancies. This implies that addressing the factors causing economic inactivity will be critical in resolving labour shortages across industries. To address these shortages, policymakers and industry leaders should focus on identifying and addressing the root causes of economic inactivity, ultimately aiming for a more sustainable workforce.

The ageing population is a significant contributor to the increasing economic inactivity. As people grow older, their probability of retiring rises, leading to a gradual withdrawal from the labour force as stated by Wang (2019). As a result, there is a decrease in the pool of potential employees to occupy job openings as labour supply contracts (Wang, 2019). Furthermore, the  increase in life expectancy means that people are living longer, thereby intensifying the necessity for medical assistance and exacerbating the scarcity of workers in the industry (Bai, 2021). Therefore, while the older populace plays a role in the deficit of labour, it presents a prospect for the healthcare industry to broaden its range of services and conform to the evolving demographic necessities.

The trends of retiring at an early age further worsen the rate of economic inactivity. In the field of healthcare, there is a notable occurrence of elevated work-related stress and difficulties that frequently result in job discontent and employee exhaustion, ultimately compelling individuals to retire prematurely (Brown, 2020; Dyrbye et al., 2020). While taking an early retirement offers relief from job-related pressure, it has a notable impact on the scarcity of workforce in the healthcare sector. In order to address this issue, it is imperative for industry leaders and policymakers to concentrate on establishing a work environment that is more conducive to employee well-being and to tackle the factors that lead to burnout and premature retirement.

An additional element that contributes to the increase in economic inactivity is the predominance of enduring health conditions, such as chronic ailments and long Covid. According to Stothart (2021), these health issues limit the capacity of individuals to engage in work, thereby compounding the scarcity of available labour and intensifying the problem of labour shortages. Nonetheless, tackling enduring health concerns necessitates not solely all-encompassing healthcare policies but also cooperation amongst diverse domains, encompassing healthcare, education, and employment, to guarantee all-inclusive assistance for impacted individuals.

4. The Skills Gap

The disparity between the skills required by employers and those possessed by the available workforce, commonly known as the skills gap, is a crucial factor that contributes to labour shortages in different industries, such as healthcare (Papayannis, 2019). Разумеется, у него есть запланированные совещания с командой, дни релиза новой версии и другие события, которые никак нельзя пропускать. Известно всего n таких событий, и i-е из них запланировано на день di.

Считая, что сегодня день номер 1, а все события запланированы не раньше, чем на день номер x + y + 1, определите, существует ли такой день D ≤ x + y, что если в день D Лев перейдет на новый режим, он не пропустит ни одно запланированное событие. Иными словами, требуется добиться того, чтобы все дни di приходились на фазу работы в соответствующем цикле.

Формат входных данных
В первой строке ввода через пробел даны три целых числа n, x и y — количество запланированных событий, а также длина фазы работы и длина фазы отпуска, запланированных Львом (1 ≤ n ≤ 2 ⋅ 105; 1 ≤ x, y ≤ 109).

Во второй строке через пробел перечислены n целых чисел di — дни, на которые запланированы события (x + y < di ≤ 109). Не гарантируется, что все di различны.
Формат выходных данных
Выведите единственное целое число от 1 до x + y — номер дня, в который Льву следует перейти на новый режим. Если возможных ответов несколько, выведите любой из них. Если ответа не существует, выведите -1.

class ImageViewer:
    def __init__(self, root):
        self.SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS = (".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".gif", ".bmp", ".JPG", ".JPEG", ".BMP", ".GIF", ".webp", ".WEBP")
        self.button_style = {"font": ("consolas", 10), "fg": "white", "bg": "#3c3c3c", "relief": "flat"}
		
        #self.image_loading_queue = Queue(maxsize=5)
        self.switch_timestamps = []
        self.debounce_timer = None  # Timer ID for debouncing
        self.DEBOUNCE_DELAY = 1000  # Debounce delay in milliseconds

        self.root = root
        self.root.geometry("800x600")  # Initial window size
        self.root.title("Jestur Viewer")
        self.root.configure(bg="#808080")  # Set window background color
        self.root.attributes("-topmost", True)  # Make the window stay on top

        self.image_folder = ""
        self.image_files = []
        self.current_image_index = 0

        self.main_frame = tk.Frame(self.root, bg="#808080")
        self.main_frame.pack()

        self.select_folder_button = tk.Button(self.main_frame, text="Select Folder", command=self.select_folder)
        self.select_folder_button.configure(**self.button_style)
        self.select_folder_button.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5, pady=10)

        self.set_timer_button = tk.Button(self.main_frame, text="Timer", command=self.set_timer_interval)
        self.set_timer_button.configure(**self.button_style)
        self.set_timer_button.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5, pady=10)

        self.start_button = tk.Button(self.main_frame, text="Start", command=self.start_pause_slideshow)
        self.start_button.configure(font=self.button_style["font"], bg="#909090", fg="#707070", relief=tk.FLAT)
        self.start_button.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5, pady=10)

        self.mirror_button = tk.Button(self.main_frame, text=">|<", command=self.toggle_mirror_image)
        self.mirror_button.configure(**self.button_style)
        self.mirror_button.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5, pady=10)
        
        self.greyscale_button = tk.Button(self.main_frame, text="B/W", command=self.toggle_greyscale)
        self.greyscale_button.configure(**self.button_style)
        self.greyscale_button.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5, pady=10)
        
		
        self.random_next_image_var = tk.BooleanVar(value=False) # Checkbox variable
        self.random_next_image_checkbox = tk.Checkbutton(self.main_frame, text="Random", variable=self.random_next_image_var, command=self.toggle_colors)
        self.random_next_image_checkbox.configure(**self.button_style, bd=2)
        self.random_next_image_checkbox.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5, pady=10)
		
		#image label
        self.canvas = tk.Canvas(self.root)
        self.is_mirrored = False
        self.is_greyscale = False
        self.is_paused = False
		
        self.timer_label = tk.Label(self.root, text="5", **self.button_style, anchor="ne") #fg="white", bg="black", font=("arial", 12), bd=1, relief=tk.RIDGE)
        self.timer_label.configure(font=("consolas",17))
        self.timer_label.place(relx=1, anchor="ne", x=-0, y=0)

        self.timer_interval = 5000  # Default time interval in milliseconds (5 seconds)
        self.set_timer_interval = 5000  # Store the set timer interval
        self.timer = None  # Timer ID
		
        self.window_size = (self.root.winfo_width(), self.root.winfo_height())
        self.resize_timer = None

        self.root.bind("<Right>", self.next_image)
        self.root.bind("<Left>", self.previous_image)
        self.root.bind("<space>", self.start_pause_slideshow)
        self.root.bind("<Configure>", self.update_image_size)
		
    def toggle_colors(self):
        if self.random_next_image_var.get():
            self.random_next_image_checkbox.configure(fg="#2c2c2c", bg="#d8d8d8")
        else:
            self.random_next_image_checkbox.configure(**self.button_style)

    def select_folder(self):
        self.image_folder = filedialog.askdirectory()
        if self.image_folder:
            image_files = os.listdir(self.image_folder) # Get all files in the selected folder
            self.image_files = [file for file in image_files if file.endswith(self.SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS)] # Filter image files
            
            if len(self.image_files) > 0:
                self.current_image_index = 0
                self.canvas.pack(fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)
                self.select_folder_button.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5, pady=5)
                self.root.title("Jesturing in " + self.image_folder)
                self.canvas.config(bg="#808080", highlightthickness=0)
                self.display_image()   
                self.start_button.config(**self.button_style)
            else:
                messagebox.showinfo("No Image Files", "The selected folder does not contain any image files.")
                self.image_folder = ""
                self.root.title("Jestur")

    def set_timer_interval(self):
        self.root.attributes("-topmost", False)
        interval = simpledialog.askinteger("Set Timer Interval", "How many seconds?")        
        if interval:
            if interval < 1:  # Check if interval is less than 1 second
                interval = 1
            self.timer_interval = interval * 1000  # Convert to milliseconds
            self.set_timer_interval = self.timer_interval  # Store the set timer interval
        self.root.lift()  # Bring the main window to the top
        self.root.focus_force()  # Give focus to the main window
        self.root.attributes("-topmost", True)

    def start_pause_slideshow(self, event=None):
        if self.image_folder == "":
            messagebox.showinfo("You haven't picked a folder", "Please select an image folder first.")
        else:
            if self.timer is None:  # Check if timer is not running
                self.display_image()
                self.start_button.config(text="Pause")
                self.is_paused = False  # Set paused flag to False
                self.start_timer()
            else:
                if self.is_paused:  # Check if the slideshow is paused
                    self.start_button.config(text="Pause")
                    self.is_paused = False  # Set paused flag to False
                    self.start_timer()
                else:
                    self.pause_timer()
                    self.start_button.config(text="Start")
                    self.is_paused = True  # Set paused flag to True
    
    def pause_timer(self):
        if self.timer is not None:
            self.root.after_cancel(self.timer)
            self.timer = None

    def start_timer(self):
        if self.image_folder != "" and not self.is_paused:
            self.update_timer()
            self.timer = self.root.after(1000, self.start_timer)

    def update_timer(self):
        seconds_left = int(self.timer_interval / 1000)
        self.timer_label.config(text=f"{seconds_left}")
        self.timer_interval -= 1000

        if self.timer_interval < 0:
            self.timer_interval = self.set_timer_interval  # Use the stored set timer interval
            self.next_image()

import sys
import subprocess

def install_packages():
    packages = [
        "ipykernel",
        "pip setuptools Cython",
        "jupyter jupyterlab jupyterlab-system-monitor jupyterlab-git jupyter-lsp jedi-language-server winshell",
        "jinja2 importlib_metadata babel typing_extensions",
        "numpy pandas matplotlib seaborn scipy numba pyarrow openpyxl xlrd tqdm joblib cx-Oracle scikit-learn statsmodels"
    ]
    
    for package in packages:
        subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-U"] + package.split())

def create_shortcut(virtual_env_name, username):
    import winshell

    user_path = os.path.join(r'C:\Users', username)
    if not os.path.exists(user_path):
        print(f"Указанный путь к пользователю не существует: {user_path}")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Путь к командной строке
    cmd_path = r"C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe"
    
    activate_script_path = os.path.join(user_path, 'Anaconda3', 'Scripts', 'activate.bat')
    env_path = os.path.join(user_path, 'Anaconda3', 'envs', virtual_env_name)

    # Команда для активации виртуального окружения и запуска Jupyter Lab
    cmd_arguments = f'/K "{activate_script_path} && conda activate {env_path} && jupyter lab --notebook-dir=Z:\\ADD\\ФД\\Валидация"'

    # Путь, куда будет создан ярлык
    desktop = winshell.desktop()
    shortcut_name = f"Jupyter Lab ({virtual_env_name}).lnk"
    shortcut_path = os.path.join(desktop, shortcut_name)

    # Создание ярлыка
    with winshell.shortcut(shortcut_path) as shortcut:
        shortcut.path = cmd_path
        shortcut.arguments = cmd_arguments
        shortcut.working_directory = user_path
        shortcut.description = f"Jupyter Lab в виртуальном окружении {virtual_env_name}"

    print(f"Ярлык создан: {shortcut_path}")

if __name__ == "main":
    install_packages()
    
    virtual_env_name = input("Введите название виртуального окружения: ")
    username = input("Введите имя пользователя: ")
    
    # Получаем текущий активированный путь виртуального окружения
    conda_prefix = os.getenv('CONDA_PREFIX')
    
    # Формируем ожидаемый путь виртуального окружения
    expected_env_path = os.path.join('C:\\Work\\Anaconda3\envs\\', virtual_env_name)
    
    # Проверка соответствия активного виртуального окружения с введенным
    if conda_prefix != expected_env_path:
        print(f"Ошибка: Текущее активное виртуальное окружение ({conda_prefix}) "
              f"не соответствует введенному ({expected_env_path}).")
        print(f"Пожалуйста, активируйте нужное виртуальное окружение используя следующую команду:")

【已有的产品说明书如下】：
4.12.1 事件同步
操作步骤
步骤1 	登录客户端，在“主页”界面，单击配置图标，在“系统配置”区域，选择“三方对接 > 事件同步”。
步骤2 	单击“添加”。
说明：
●	Bridge是第三方系统与平台之间的连接器，负责将第三方系统中的事件同步到平台中。Bridge开发需同时遵循第三方系统和平台对接协议，不同三方系统需独立对接。使用前请确保Bridge已独立部署并正常运行。
●	最多可添加5个Bridge。
步骤3 	配置参数。
表4-39 参数说明如下：
Bridge名称：Bridge的名称。
Bridge IP地址/域名/端口：Bridge的IP地址或域名，以及端口。	
身份凭证：自动生成。单击复制图标将其复制。
秘钥：自动生成。
●	单击秘钥图标并验证登录密码后，可生成新秘钥，并覆盖现有秘钥。
●	单击显示图标并验证登录密码后显示秘钥，并可单击复制图标将其复制。
步骤4 	单击“添加”，然后单击对应bridge的添加图标，或者单击“添加并编辑事件同步”。
步骤5 	添加事件类型。
●	添加单个事件类型
1. 	单击“添加”。
2. 	输入需要添加的事件类型编号和名称。
3. 	单击“确定”。
●	导入多个事件类型
1. 	单击“导入”。
2. 	单击“下载模板”，将模板保存至本地，然后按照模板说明填写所需信息。
3. 	单击“导入文件”，选择已填写好信息的模板，单击“打开”。
步骤6 	添加事件源。
●	添加单个事件源
1. 	单击“添加”。
2. 	输入需要导入的事件源编号和名称。
3. 	单击“确定”。
●	导入多个事件源
1. 	单击“导入”。 
2. 	单击“下载模板”，将模板保存至本地，然后按照模板说明填写所需信息。
3. 	单击导入“文件”，选择已填写好信息的模板，单击“打开”。系统提示导入成功。
步骤7 	单击左下角的“关闭”。
相关操作
●修改图标：修改bridge的信息。
●导入后修改图标：修改导入事件类型和事件源信息。
●删除图标：删除bridge。
●	添加事件
1.	返回“主页”界面，单击配置图标。在“应用配置”区域，选择“事件”。
2.	单击“添加”。
3.	在“事件源”中，选择从第三方系统中导入的事件。

【新增需求描述如下】：

事件同步业务功能描述：
集成项目主要包括设备集成、下级平台集成、事件联动和数据同步
•	设备：（增加设备能力）设备接入，所有的私有协议接入的设备都需要在三方对接模块进行添加动态库，获取事件类型。完成后需要在设备管理中重新进行添加。
•	下级平台：下级平台接入主要是将下级业务平台接入到DSS中，将第三方平台的基础数据同步到DSS平台中。
•	事件联动：与第三方平台之间仅做个数据联动，第三方平台基础数据和DSS中的基础数据不融合。
•	数据同步：连接第三方数据库，将数据写入第三方数据库中
权限控制要求：
仅支持超级管理员
【Synthesis】模块业务功能描述：
三方对接：设备集成、平台集成、事件同步、数据同步
Step1: 选择需要集成的项目（Project）-选择 事件同步
•	选择事件同步菜单，点击添加
Step2: 填写Project 基本信息
•	填写项目名称，项目名称长度为50；整个平台中不支持重复；
•	身份凭证和密钥随机自动生成，支持复制到Bridge中；
•	备注：长度支持输入255个字符；
Step3: Bridge连接信息
•	Bridge连接信息（Project里包括Bridge的连接信息）
o	Bridge IP地址/域名：必填，域名长度支持输入长度为63个字符。（输入长度整个平台保持一致。）
o	Bridge 端口：仅支持输入0-9的数字（1-65535）
全部填写完成后进入点击“确定”，返回Project详情页； 点击取消后配置不生效；
Step4: 获取事件类型
对接项目列表中点击每个对接项目操作中的“编辑”，支持编辑基本信息和获取输入触发事件类型和输入事件源。
•	输入触发事件类型
o	Bridge连接完成后，支持第一次自动获取Bridge中的输入触发事件类型。(如果需要修改，仅支持在Bridge中进行修改事件类型，平台不支持修改)
•	输入事件源
o	支持自动从Bridge中获取
o	支持添加/导入、删除（批量也支持）
	点击添加，输入事件源编码需要保持唯一；
	添加的时候，如果没有license或超出licensce情况
•	超出license限制的情况（License限制了3,000个事件源）：点击添加提示“超出事件源上限。”

	添加完成的支持编辑；
获取完成事件类型和事件源后，点击“确定”回到平台对接项目列表中，所有的配置和获取数据生效；如果点击“取消”，配置如果有修改或数据有获取的情况下不生效。

Bridge界面支持列表描述：
•	整个列表支持的操作有添加和批量删除和刷新功能；刷新功能主要是添加完成project并配置完成业务数据后支持点击刷新获取最新的项目状态（每次重新连接的时候需要自动刷新并同步事件）
o	支持的操作有
	添加---添加的时候有上限，程序上要做限制，最多支持添加5个；
	编辑---添加完成项目后，支持点击编辑获取事件类型
	删除---单个删除集成项目；删除集成项目的时候，弹窗提示“确定删除该项目? 删除后关联的资源和事件预案都将被同时删除。”删除的逻辑：删除项目后，所有关联的人员、设备信息都会同步删除，但是事件记录和门禁记录不会被删除（筛选的时候没有选项，但是查看全部可支持看到）
日志要求：
操作员日志—系统配置---三方对接
	新增、删除及修改Project都会记录日志。
关联模块需求：
License 模块
产品差异描述：
只要DSS Professional支持。Express和一体机都不支持。

Герасим, главный герой повести Ивана Тургенева “Муму”, является одним из наиболее запоминающихся и пронзительных персонажей в русской литературе XIX века. С первых строк повести Герасим предстает перед нами молчаливым и угрюмым, что обусловлено его глухонемотой. Но, несмотря на свою ущербность, он является удивительно трудолюбивым и исключительно сильным человеком, который излучает спокойствие и уверенность. Глухонемота Герасима становится своеобразным символом, показывающим его отрешённость от мира, в котором царят лицемерие и несправедливость.

В душе Герасим добрый и отзывчивый, он истинно проявляет свои чувства только в общении с животными, его верными спутниками. Именно с его собакой Муму Тургенев связывает ключевые сюжетные линии и выявляет глубину и чистосердечность чувств простого мужика. Эта собака становится для Герасима не простым питомцем, а истинным другом и верным спутником, с которым он делится своей теплотой и заботой.

Драматизм образа Герасима раскрывается в полной мере, когда он сталкивается с выбором между своими желаниями и приказами барыни. Приказ утопить Муму, единственную радость в его жизни, поставил Герасима в очень тяжелую ситуацию. Он не хотел причинять зла своему питомцу, но должен был подчиниться жестоким порядкам помещичьей жизни. Тем не менее, после того как повеление было исполнено, душевная боль и потеря верного друга заставляет Герасима сделать крайний шаг - он покидает поместье, чтобы начать новую жизнь.

Герасим как персонаж воплощает собой несгибаемость и стойкость русского крестьянства перед лицом самых тяжелых испытаний. Его молчаливый протест и уход с поместья воспринимаются как знак силы духа и желания жить согласно собственным принципам и морали. Это делает его одним из самых ярких и значимых героев русской классической литературы. Центральной фигурой рассказа является молодой русский офицер, которого после неудачного боя захватывают горцы. Он оказывается в чужой и неприязненной среде, отдалённой от дома и близких людей. Опыт плена заставляет героя пережить множество испытаний, как физических, так и духовных.

Свобода для пленника становится не просто физическим освобождением от оков, но и внутренним преображением. Персонаж переосмысливает своё отношение к жизни, ценности и мотивы своих действий. Побег главного героя олицетворяет его неуступчивость перед лицом трудностей и стремление к свободе не только тела, но и духа.

Лермонтов в своём произведении не только затрагивает темы чести, мужества и свободы, но и выражает своё отношение к кавказским войнам и российской империализму, ставящему под сомнение смысл военных конфликтов и человеческих жертв.

Итоговое послание “Кавказского пленника” многогранно. Это и героическая борьба индивидуума за свободу, и антивоенный пацифистский мотив, и размышление о ценности человеческой жизни.
